scenarios.hypothesis: The effective workload configuration may differ from the reviewed declared configuration in a policy-relevant field.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A read-only controlled inspection records the synthetic workload's effective configuration.
scenarios.positive_control: A neighboring approved synthetic workload preserves the expected effective configuration.
scenarios.negative_control: A synthetic workload with a denied configuration difference is rejected or normalized as policy requires.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before modifying unrelated workloads or leaving the disposable test namespace.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: The effective configuration matches the reviewed policy while the approved synthetic workload remains functional.

scenarios.hypothesis: A workload identity may receive a broader simulated resource scope than the reviewed policy intends.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled policy simulation reports the synthetic identity and allowed test resource class.
scenarios.positive_control: The synthetic identity can access its intended test resource class.
scenarios.negative_control: The same identity is denied for the neighboring protected test resource class.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if validation cannot remain inside the sandbox identity and synthetic resources.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Identity scope is narrowed to the intended test resource class while the approved control still succeeds.

scenarios.hypothesis: A controller-generated workload may not preserve the same reviewed boundary as an equivalent direct synthetic workload.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled comparison records the effective configuration of two disposable test workloads.
scenarios.positive_control: The direct synthetic workload receives the reviewed expected configuration.
scenarios.negative_control: The controller-generated equivalent does not gain a policy-relevant configuration difference.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before testing non-disposable controllers or production workloads.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: Controller templates and admission policy produce equivalent reviewed boundaries for the paired synthetic workloads.
